name: APDS-9301 ambient light (lux) sensor
description: Broadcom/Avago light-to-digital converter with a broadband (visible + IR) and an infrared-only photodiode, two integrating 16-bit ADCs and an I2C interface (up to 400 kHz); lux is computed from the two channels with the datasheet's empirical formula. Chip and board run on 2.7-3.6 V only (no regulator, no level shifting). Sold as: SparkFun Ambient Light Sensor Breakout - APDS-9301 (SEN-14350), 5-pin header INT, GND, 3.3V, SDA, SCL with 4.7k I2C pull-ups and a 10k INT pull-up to 3.3V, I2C address 0x39 (address jumper on the back selects 0x29 or 0x49).
eli5: Tells your board how bright the light is, in lux, like a camera's light meter.

pins.name: INT
pins.description: Interrupt output, open-drain, active low (10k pull-up to 3.3V on board); not needed for basic use

pins.name: 3.3V
pins.description: Supply, 2.7-3.6 V straight to the chip (no regulator): never connect to 5 V

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (4.7k pull-up to 3.3V on board), 3.6 V max

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (4.7k pull-up to 3.3V on board), 3.6 V max

supplierQuery: APDS-9301 ambient light sensor breakout I2C
buildNotes: Power the board from 3.3 V only: the APDS-9301 is rated 2.7-3.6 V (absolute max 3.8 V) and the board has no regulator or level shifter, so a 5 V Arduino needs a level translator.

Every register access starts with a command byte 0x80 | register. Power up by writing 0x03 to 0x80 and read 0x80 back: it returns 0x03 when the chip is answering. ID register 0x8A has 0101 in its upper nibble.

Timing register (0x81): bit 4 = gain 16x, bits 1:0 = integration 00 13.7 ms, 01 101 ms, 10 402 ms (power-on default 0x02 = 1x, 402 ms). Wait one full integration after power-up or a change before reading.
Read channel 0 (visible + IR) with Read Word command 0xAC and channel 1 (IR) with 0xAE; each is low byte first.

Lux comes from both channels with the datasheet's CH1/CH0 formula, characterised at 16x gain and 402 ms: scale counts by 16 at 1x gain and by 322/81 or 322/11 at 101 ms or 13.7 ms. Full scale is 65535 at 402 ms, 37177 at 101 ms, 5047 at 13.7 ms: a full-scale count means saturated.

Address: 0x39 with the back jumper open. The datasheet gives ADDR SEL to GND = 0x29 and to VDD = 0x49; SparkFun's labels for the two jumper sides disagree, so confirm with an I2C scan after closing one.
sources: https://cdn.sparkfun.com/assets/learn_tutorials/6/8/6/header_highlighted.png (silkscreen top to bottom: INT, GND, 3.3V, SDA, SCL)
https://cdn.sparkfun.com/assets/9/c/2/4/9/APDS-9301_Breakout_v10.pdf (schematic: J1 GND/VCC/SDA/SCL, J2 INT, 4.7k SDA/SCL and 10k INT pull-ups to VCC)

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from apds9301 import APDS9301

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = APDS9301(i2c)  # gain 1x, 402 ms
while True:
    ch0, ch1 = sensor.raw()
    lux = sensor.lux()
    if lux is None:
        print('CH0=%d CH1=%d Lux=saturated' % (ch0, ch1))
    else:
        print('CH0=%d CH1=%d Lux=%.1f' % (ch0, ch1, lux))
    time.sleep(1)
